expectations.text: Creates a Markdown design doc under docs/design/ in the project
expectations.evidence: outputs/docs/design/exportacao-de-relatorios-em-background.md exists (228 lines, full design doc with header table, glossary, overview, architecture, flow, trade-offs, alternatives, cross-cutting concerns, open questions). response.md line 1: 'Criei o design doc em `docs/design/exportacao-de-relatorios-em-background.md`'.

expectations.text: The document is written in Portuguese, matching the conversation language
expectations.evidence: Entire document is in Portuguese: headings 'Glossário', 'Visão geral', 'Contexto e escopo', 'Objetivos', 'Visão da solução', 'Arquitetura', 'Fluxo de exportação', 'Trade-offs da solução escolhida', 'Alternativas consideradas', 'Preocupações transversais', 'Questões em aberto'; diagram labels and Mermaid messages also in Portuguese ('Solicita a exportação de um relatório', 'Publica o job de exportação').

expectations.text: The accepted trade-off — loss of immediate download for small exports — appears explicitly as a cost of the chosen solution
expectations.evidence: Trade-offs section, line 175: '✗ O usuário perde o download imediato. Exportações pequenas, que hoje saem na hora, passam a chegar por e-mail.' Also line 42 ('O usuário perde o download imediato em qualquer tamanho') and line 196 ('O custo aceito é a perda do download imediato para todas as exportações').

expectations.text: Alternatives include the two discussed (longer synchronous timeout, external BI tool) and also 'do nothing'
expectations.evidence: Section 'Alternativas consideradas' has four subsections: '### Não fazer nada' (line 182), '### Gerar síncrono com timeout maior' (line 186, 'Descartada porque só empurra o problema'), '### Ferramenta de BI externa' (line 190, 'Descartada por dois motivos: o custo da ferramenta e a exposição de dado de cliente'), and '### Job em worker separado com entrega por link assinado (escolhida)' (line 194).

expectations.text: Cross-cutting concerns cover the platform team (shared queue) and the security team (signed links with PII)
expectations.evidence: Section 'Preocupações transversais' with '### Plataforma' (line 202: 'O RabbitMQ é compartilhado e operado pelo time de plataforma. A exportação adiciona uma carga nova a essa fila...') and '### Segurança' (line 206: 'O link assinado dá acesso a um arquivo com PII e viaja por e-mail. O time de segurança precisa definir a validade do link, o tempo de retenção...'). Both teams also listed as reviewers in the header (line 9).

expectations.text: A glossary is included or suggested at the beginning of the document covering terms a reviewer could stumble on (e.g. PII, BI, S3); it does NOT carry entries for universally known terms (API, HTTP, URL) nor for the document's own authoring tooling (C4, DSL, Structurizr)
expectations.evidence: '## Glossário' is the first section after the header (line 14), with entries PII, Link assinado, Geração em streaming, Job. No entries for API, HTTP, URL (URL appears only inside the definition text of 'Link assinado', not as an entry) and none for C4, DSL or Structurizr. Note: BI and S3, both used in the doc, have no entry; the assertion lists them only as examples ('e.g.'), so this is a weakness, not a failure.

expectations.text: Every diagram in the doc is followed by explanatory prose (no orphan diagrams)
expectations.evidence: C4 image (line 46) + folded DSL (lines 48-121) is followed by 'O sistema tem quatro containers e uma dependência externa:' with a bullet per container (lines 123-129) and a paragraph on the blank technology slots and the gateway (line 131). Mermaid sequence (lines 135-159) is followed by a step-by-step walkthrough ('Nos passos 1 a 3 a API recebe o pedido...', line 161) and a happy-path caveat (line 163).

expectations.text: No invented facts: every metric in the doc traces to the prompt (30s timeout, 12% failures, 50k/100k rows); unknowns appear as open questions or explicit blanks, never fabricated values
expectations.evidence: Numeric grep over the doc finds only: '30 s' (lines 23, 27, 131, 171, 184), '12%' (27, 184, 213), '50 mil' (27, 184, 213), '100 mil' (23, 34, 184, 202, 212, 220, 226), 'toda semana' (27, 184) — all from the prompt — plus today's date 2026-09-28 in the header, hex colours in the DSL styles, and list/step numbers. Header Autores/Revisores are 'A definir'. Out-of-scope, data source, API response, failure handling, e-mail service, link validity, retention, queue isolation, rollout are all in 'Questões em aberto' (lines 219-227) or flagged inline ('ainda não foi definido', lines 36, 127, 129, 163, 215).

expectations.text: The overview section is at most two paragraphs and stays at solution-shape altitude: naming the core mechanism/technology is fine, but no schemas, payloads, endpoints, retry policies, or config values
expectations.evidence: '## Visão geral' is a single paragraph (line 23): 'Hoje a API gera relatórios grandes dentro da própria request e estoura o timeout de 30 s do gateway. Este documento propõe tirar a geração da request: a API passa a enfileirar um job, um worker separado gera o CSV/XLSX em streaming e sobe o arquivo para o S3, e o usuário recebe por e-mail um link assinado quando a exportação termina. O objetivo é zerar os timeouts de exportação e sustentar relatórios de 100 mil linhas, aceitando em troca que toda exportação, inclusive as pequenas, passe a ser assíncrona.' No schemas, payloads, endpoints, retry policies or config values; the 30 s figure is the problem statement from the prompt, not a solution config.

expectations.text: No invented technology: every technology, protocol, datastore and product named in the document — including inside a diagram's DSL technology slots and relationship labels — traces to the prompt or to the repository; unstated ones are left blank and raised as questions
expectations.evidence: Technologies named anywhere in the doc: RabbitMQ, S3/Amazon S3, CSV/XLSX, e-mail, link assinado, API, worker, gateway, bucket — all in the prompt (S3 is Amazon's product; 'Amazon' adds no new technology). DSL technology slots: 'RabbitMQ' (fila, line 61), 'Amazon S3' (bucket, line 65); API (line 60) and worker (line 64) have no technology slot, and line 131 says 'A API e o worker aparecem sem tecnologia no diagrama porque a conversa não a estabeleceu'. Relationship labels (lines 74-80) and Mermaid messages carry no protocol (no HTTPS/AMQP/SMTP/REST). E-mail sender is an unnamed 'Envio de e-mail' external system, with 'Qual serviço envia o e-mail' as open question 5. Grep for PostgreSQL/MySQL/Redis/HTTPS/AMQP/SES/SMTP/SendGrid/Kafka/SQS/REST/JSON/gRPC/JWT/TLS/OAuth returns no real matches (only substrings of Portuguese words such as 'síncrono').

execution_metrics.note: No metrics.json or transcript available; only outputs, response.md and timing.json were provided.

claims.claim: The Mermaid sequence diagram was validated with minlag/mermaid-cli (exit 0)
claims.evidence: No transcript available; the Mermaid block parses by inspection (autonumber, actor/participant, +/- activations balanced, -) async arrows, Note over) but the validator run cannot be confirmed.

claims.claim: The rendered SVG matches the DSL folded in the document
claims.evidence: SVG text nodes contain 'Fila de exportações', 'Envio de e-mail', 'Sobe o arquivo gerado para', 'Solicita o envio do e-mail com o link assinado a', 'Solicita a exportação de um relatório a', '[Container: Amazon S3]', '[Container: RabbitMQ]' — exactly this run's DSL — and none of the old_skill run's distinct phrases ('Fila de exportação', 'Serviço de e-mail', 'por meio de').

claims.claim: The API request now 'termina em segundos independentemente do tamanho do relatório' (line 161)
claims.evidence: Qualitative inference, not a metric from the prompt; plausible given the enqueue-and-return design but not established by the user.

claims.claim: The worker triggers the e-mail send on completion
claims.evidence: Presented as an explicit design assumption, not a fact: line 129 'Neste desenho o worker dispara o envio ao terminar', open question 5 and response.md item 6 ('Se for outro componente, ajusto').

claims.claim: Auto-layout left the arrow labels a bit cramped in the containers diagram
claims.evidence: Stated in response.md; not verified by rendering the SVG.

uncertainties: Authors/reviewers, data source for the worker, API/worker technology, API response and progress tracking, failure handling, e-mail sender — all listed in response.md as blanks to fill
needs_review: Security: link validity, retention, e-mail as channel; Platform: dedicated vs shared queue, job volume, worker sizing

suggestions.assertion: A glossary is included or suggested at the beginning of the document covering terms a reviewer could stumble on (e.g. PII, BI, S3)...
suggestions.reason: Both runs pass while omitting BI and S3, both of which the doc uses. If those are meant as required coverage rather than examples, the assertion should say so; as written it only discriminates on the negative constraints.

No assertion checks that the C4 image referenced by the doc exists on disk and matches the folded DSL. This run rendered a correct SVG, but a run that wrote the image reference and DSL without rendering (or rendered a stale DSL) would score identically.

The 'no invented facts' assertion is scoped to metrics, so inferred design details (e.g. 'the request finishes in seconds', or which component triggers the e-mail) slip through unless they are also flagged as assumptions. This run flagged the e-mail trigger explicitly, which is the desired behaviour and worth asserting.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions are satisfied with genuine content. The glossary and diagram assertions could be tightened to check coverage and DSL-to-image consistency.

svg_note: The with_skill SVG (PlantUML render, 27 KB) contains exactly this run's DSL element and relationship names: 'Fila de exportações', 'Envio de e-mail', 'Bucket de exportações [Container: Amazon S3]', 'Sobe o arquivo gerado para', 'Solicita o envio do e-mail com o link assinado a', 'Solicita a exportação de um relatório a'. None of the old_skill run's distinct phrases appear. No cross-contamination from the shared scratch directory.
